assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's single curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read in full with its front matter: the active_provisional V1 monograph series/genshin-impact/05 Character Monographs/GENSHIN_FURINA_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md, repository literary analysis of the Genshin Impact 7.0.0 Tier-A normalized corpus (CHS controlling, JP and EN parallel) centered on the Fontaine Archon Quest, the Furina Story Quest, profile and voice records, and later event, tabletop and direction material. Textual evidence only: the monograph records no approved audio-locator corpus. The deep readings, ledgers, specialist syntheses, locator index and claim-evidence matrix it summarizes are not curated on this subject; scene references and the few exact locators cited below are the monograph's own, and no claim rests on unread linked material. The project's readiness labels (behavioral model PARTIAL, speech text READY, performance NOT_READY) and the discovery note's 'nonauthoritative before G8' are not adopted. The corpus map was consulted for context only. No primary-source inspection was performed.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Furina from the five-century interior history (mirror promise and the scales decision, Quest 4024, revealed late but part of her knowledge at every later state) through the Fontaine arrival, the Lyney trial, the Vacher/Navia case, prophecy and Arlecchino pressure, the Poisson collapse and her trial, then the immediate post-role apartment withdrawal, the Story Quest troupe reclamation, tabletop roleplay and later artistic direction as the latest represented state. Capability states split at located changes: captive role until the Oratrice verdict ends the office; immediate post-role from the verdict until she chooses to perform for the troupe in the Story Quest; mature post-role after that choice. Within the captive role, procedural receptivity is available only after the Lyney trial. Exact diegetic ordering of later events, Talk and profile lines is not established by the evidence, and nothing after the 7.0.0 corpus is in scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives phase-ranked value hierarchies (captive: Fontaine's survival, secrecy preserving hope, role continuity above dignity and relief; mature: non-compulsion, accountability and chosen relationship above status, s24.9), named state variables (audience visibility, frame clarity, physical risk, identity exposure, collective stakes, consent, trust, debt, s28.2) and a read-frame-protect-evaluate-act-update-repair sequence (s28.3). It explains contrasts in observed behavior: overcommitment to a public theory in the Lyney trial against procedural receptivity in the Vacher case (s6), duel avoidance against Primordial Seawater (s10), refusal to act and then following the Traveler out of concern (s17.4-17.5). It predicts her mistakes: incentive-distorted reasoning, reframing instead of acknowledgment, work substituting for support, disproportionate refusal of open-ended need and the debt response (s26.11). Not A: one unaudited active-provisional monograph whose exact locators are few and whose s30 and Appendix B predictions are untested model output. Not C: the account says which variable moves her and where it stops (romance, long-term recovery, public aftermath), and the remaining uncertainty is mostly productive.

Nine developmental movements (s3), three behavioral states with high- and low-probability response lists (s28.4-28.6) and function-change tracks for theatricality, pride, fear, duty, justice, social need and identity (s25). The transitions are on the page: the Lyney-to-Vacher update, the Poisson collapse, the verdict that ends the office, the post-role void and the Story Quest choice to perform. The prospective-versus-retrospective rule (s1) keeps later revelation from erasing earlier behavior. Not A: cross-surface chronology is partial (s31.2), so the ordering of mature-phase events and of profile lines is unlocated. Not C: states and their change mechanisms are explicit and tied to named quest events.

Addressee-conditioned register rules (public stranger, familiar companion, trusted friend, adversary, artistic collaborator, person harmed by her office, s29.1-29.6), stable JP boku across registers (s19.1, s29.8), register functions for divine, courtroom, defensive, collapse, pleading, reflective, professional and recreational speech (s19), request-as-activity patterns (s19.10) and a list of speech errors to avoid (s19.11). Not B: the item quotes almost no source wording in any language (one locator for the tears-as-opera reframe, 4022/0/20/0, and the 4024/6/90 line in translation), so realization is constrained by operations rather than lexicon; the 2,364-node corpus behind the project's text-READY label is not presented in the cited item, and no acoustic evidence exists. Not D: the register rules are conditional on addressee and safety, not mere tendencies.

Apartment life, macaroni and household awkwardness, compensatory shopping (profile voice 89031), sweets, tea and shared meals as structure for companionship, boredom and novelty, and the difficulty of unstructured company (s23, s30.14). Not B: few ordinary scenes are located, and most of the mundane account in s30 and Appendix B is the monograph's own inference. Not D: the sampled behavior carries a conditional account (finite, clearly social invitations accepted; pity deflected; care converted into reciprocity).

Dyad mechanisms for the Traveler (cross-state witness outside Fontaine's expectation system), Paimon (legible feedback), Neuvillette (procedural anchor under unshared secret), Navia (consequence and accountability), Clorinde (bounded invitation without demanded vulnerability), Arlecchino (accurate perception without safety produces concealment), Charlotte and Focalors (s22), and a relationship-type matrix of what she seeks, fears, does and can become (Appendix D), with explicit safety and defensiveness conditions (D.1, D.2). The behavior differs as predicted between safe and unsafe perceivers and between wanted and needed. Not A: Lyney, Lynette and Charlotte are thin, and the monograph says Neuvillette, Traveler, Navia and Clorinde need later differential passes (s31.5). Not C: the deltas are directional and explained by safety, competence, consent and history.

Furina-owned interior evidence: the scales decision with its admitted 'why do I have to be the one to suffer' (4024/6/90/0, 4024/6/92/0), the private Poisson collapse (4022/0/8/0-14/0), the internalized commander (s16.5) and profile and character-story records of image-self fusion, fear and repayment anxiety (89024, 89032, 89044, 89204-89206). Not A: profile and story records are not placed diegetically, and much inner content for the mature state is inferred from behavior. Not C: there are multiple located focal interior sources across the captive and post-role states.

A conditional conflict policy: she avoids danger that is physically immediate, uncontrolled, adversary-imposed or unrelated to accepted duty, and acts despite fear when stakes are collective and legible, procedure contains the conflict or the role is chosen (s10.2, s10.6); she converts conflict into trial, joke or procedure (s5.1, s15.3), loses fluency when shame is weaponized (Arlecchino, s6.5) and becomes sharper and more distant with an unsafe accurate perceiver (s30.12). Public versus private correction is distinguished (s30.7-30.8). Not A: no combat-behavior corpus, and the mature-state conflict predictions are mostly inference. Not C: the escalation and avoidance conditions are located in the arrival, trials, Arlecchino scenes and her trial.

Shown deliberation, not only positions: the scales decision weighs her own suffering against Fontaine and preserves self-value (4024/6/90/0-92/0, s9); after Poisson she considers giving up and refuses because she cannot choose fate for everyone (s9.4, s15.1); she decides to face Poisson without demanding forgiveness (s17.7); and her art ethics separate shaped emotion from emotional dumping and performer consent (s18.4). The monograph keeps open whether the political costs of secrecy were avoidable (s8.4). Not A: the mature-phase hierarchy is partly inferred and the secrecy counterfactual is unresolved. Not C: the criteria and their phase-dependent ranking are evidenced across several decisions.

Humor typed by function (defensive, dominant, affiliative, artistic, s20), imaginary companions (character story 89206, Crabaletta), reversible tabletop roleplay (s18.7) and limits where humor invalidates another's need (s20.7). Not B: few located instances, and no account of what fails to amuse her or how play varies across named interlocutors. Not D: the functions are conditioned on exposure and familiarity.

The monograph declares its source lock (6,340 Furina-relevant nodes, 2,364 attributed, 213 StoryUnits, twelve source classes) and its own open boundary: partial main-story joins, partial cross-surface chronology, TextMap gaps, no audio corpus, incomplete relationships and public aftermath (s1, s31). Not B: a single active-provisional synthesis, few exact locators in the cited item, and the locator index and claim-evidence matrix that would make its claims checkable are not curated on this subject. Not D: coverage of the main arc, Story Quest, profiles and later events is explicit.

Trait calibration with counterevidence for each trait and a rejected global narcissism model (Appendix A), explicit rejections of the fake/true-self mask model (s11), of 'frivolous', 'incompetent', 'fraud' and 'martyr' readings (s27), of a fearless or paralyzed Furina (s10.6), and the monograph's own rejection of a complete mature behavioral model (Appendix E). Not A: counterexamples are drawn from the same synthesis and are untested. Not C: the constraints are affirmative and tied to observed behavior, not gaps restated as limits.

Claims are routed to captive, immediate post-crisis and mature states (s28.4-28.6) and the Lyney/Vacher order is used as a learning boundary. Not B: the stable priors (s28.1) and many trait claims are cross-state, the profile and voice-line evidence relied on for interior claims carries no diegetic placement, and the ordering of later events is unlocated (s31.2). Not D: the state split itself is explicit and grounded in named events.

conditions: Illustrative reconstruction at a named state, never attributed quotation; canon wording is retrieved from the source, which this evidence barely quotes.

Registers limited to the sampled ones: divine public, courtroom, defensive bravado, private collapse, trial pleading, reflective post-crisis, professional direction and recreational roleplay with meta-commentary.
Keep stable JP boku and persistent theatricality; avoid constant bombast, uniformly subdued mature Furina, two grammatical selves, and direct statement of need before safety is tested (s19.11).
Textual register only: no claims about delivery, timing or vocal performance.
scenario_readiness.note: The addressee rules, register functions and speech errors constrain register selection enough for illustrative use; the monograph's own example lines (C.3, C.4) are labeled reconstruction, not source. Not READY: the cited item quotes almost no source wording and no acoustic evidence exists. Not NOT_READY: register choice is evidenced as conditional on addressee, safety and chosen role.

conditions: Change one variable at a time from a named state (audience visibility, frame clarity, physical risk, identity exposure, collective stakes, consent, trust, debt) and state it; the output must differ across them, including wanted versus needed and safe versus unsafe perceiver.
Captive-role scenarios keep secrecy beyond her jurisdiction: she does not disclose for relief even to a trusted interlocutor.

A new existential crisis for mature Furina is a separate, lower-confidence condition: the evidence does not settle whether bounded-responsibility principles hold against the old duty reflex at that scale.
A transfer to a comparable friend or collaborator outside the sampled relationships is a separate, lower-confidence condition justified only by the Appendix D type matrix.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named state: captive role before or after the Lyney trial, the Poisson collapse and trial, immediate post-role withdrawal before the Story Quest performance choice, or mature post-role after it; five-century memories belong to her at every state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: The Traveler, Paimon, Neuvillette, Navia, Clorinde, Arlecchino, the Fontaine public, troupe or film collaborators, or a person harmed by her office, each in the relationship the evidence samples at that state.
setting_constraints: Fontaine courts, the Palais and public spectacle, prophecy pressure, her apartment and ordinary city life, troupe, tabletop and production settings.
No combat-centered, romance or cross-world settings without a stated assumption, and no content from after the 7.0.0 corpus.

scenario_readiness.note: The state variables, phase hierarchies and safety conditions support bounded counterfactuals; the s30 predictions and Appendix B matrix are untested model output and set expectations, not evidence.

conditions: Mature or immediate post-role Furina in finite, clearly social activities with the Traveler, Paimon, Clorinde, Navia or collaborators.
Unstructured idleness, money detail and household routine beyond the sampled awkwardness are lower-confidence.
scenario_readiness.note: Apartment life, food, shopping, tea and activity-mediated invitations are sampled. Not READY: few ordinary scenes are located and the mundane account is largely inferential.

conditions: Self-cost against collective survival under a captive-role frame, accountability to people harmed by her office, consent and boundaries in artistic work, and bounded versus open-ended requests in the mature state.
Whether secrecy's political costs were avoidable, and mature choices under a new existential threat, stay open.
scenario_readiness.note: The scales decision, the refusal to give up and the art-consent standard support narrow prediction with the phase-ranked hierarchy.

The monograph affirmatively records that the evidence does not support romance-specific prediction and leaves the relationship type open (Appendix B, 'close friend falls in love'); friendship and activity-mediated closeness are assessed under other scenarios.

conditions: Captive-role trial and public-authority conduct with incentive-distorted reasoning before the Lyney correction and narrower certainty after it.
Mature artistic consulting, direction and critique: precise craft reasons, protection of performer agency and credit distribution.
Institutional office beyond the trials, and mentoring, are lower-confidence; technical mastery of the prophecy mechanism is outside her knowledge.
scenario_readiness.note: Courtroom conduct across the two trials and post-role consulting and direction are sampled with stated incentive conditions.

known_limits.statement: All claims rest on one active-provisional V1 monograph that summarizes uncurated readings, ledgers and evidence indexes; its novel-situation predictions and scenario matrix are model output, not evidence.
No approved audio-locator corpus supports delivery, timing or vocal performance; textual register claims are stronger than acoustic ones (s31.4).
Main-story joins and cross-surface chronology are partial, so later events, Talk lines and profile records are not diegetically ordered (s31.1-31.2).
Romance-specific behavior is unsupported and the relevant relationship type is left open.
She lacked knowledge and control of the prophecy mechanism, the Oratrice and Indemnitium; do not model captive Furina as technically sovereign or able to explain the plan (s8.1-8.2).
Long-term recovery and the public political aftermath are not established; the mature state is substantial reintegration, not a final endpoint (s31.6-31.7).
Whether the political and relational costs of secrecy were avoidable is left open (s8.4).
The cited item gives exact locators for only a handful of scenes and profile records; most claims cite scenes by name, and the locator index and claim-evidence matrix are not curated on this subject.
No realization audit or native-speaker check of generated Furina dialogue exists in the evidence, and the item quotes little source wording.
No combat-behavior corpus, and Lyney, Lynette, Charlotte and the wider post-role network are thinly covered.
